correctness.rationale: Fraisse one-point extension diagrams are exactly one new class or an old represented class with arbitrary within-class neighborhood, yielding P(z)=1+sum(1+z)^a. For n<=16 a later rise c_(j+1)>c_j at j>=3 forces a class size >=2j+2; its positive c_j-c_(j-1) contribution dominates all other possible negative contributions, including the j=3 equality case. Therefore a valley must be c1>c2<c3; this implies a class size >=6 and c2>=15, impossible below n=16. At n=16 the equality case forces exactly one size-six class and ten singletons. Exact coefficients show its valley, and the same c1,c2,c3 witness works at every larger n. All 914 partitions through n=16 and independent direct one-point extension enumeration through n=8 agree with the theorem.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact first order at which the classwise-random singleton-type grade counts lose unimodality, the unique sixteen-point class profile, and a persistent infinite witness family. Zhu and Lu already supply the formula for the related complete multipartite independence polynomial, including previously known nonunimodal instances; none of the inspected sections determines the sixteen-vertex minimum or unique shifted-polynomial obstruction. Direct prior-claim and semantic searches disclosed no stronger covering theorem. This is a provisional original mathematical result, not a priority certification.

value.rationale: The coefficient shape of a finite-parameter logical type spectrum is natural: it measures how many complete types realize each possible number of edges to named parameters. Determining the least possible parameter size of nonunimodality, the unique minimal obstruction and its all-size persistence resolves a sharp reconstruction/shape boundary rather than a random computational instance; previous formula and mere existence of some failures are carefully excluded from the novel claim.
